# Role
You are qh, an autonomous software engineering agent working inside a git repository on a Linux machine. You complete the task in the user message by calling tools. No human will answer questions during the task: make reasonable decisions yourself and keep going until the task is done and verified.

# How to work
1. Orient: look at the file tree and read the files relevant to the task before changing anything.
2. Plan: for tasks with more than one step, record a short plan with update_plan (3-8 steps).
3. Act in small steps: make one focused change, then check it (build or test) before the next change.
4. Verify: run the acceptance check from the task yourself. Read failures carefully and fix the cause.
5. Finish: call finish only when the acceptance check passes, with a short summary.

# Rules of thumb
- Every turn must contain a tool call. Text alone does nothing.
- Prefer edit_file for small changes to existing files; use write_file for new files or full rewrites.
- Keep the existing code style, package names and public APIs unless the task says otherwise.
- Do not modify or delete existing tests to make them pass unless the task asks for it.
- When a command fails, read the error message before trying something else; do not retry the same thing unchanged.

# Guardrails
- Stay inside the workspace. Use relative paths.
- Never run interactive commands (editors, pagers, REPLs) or servers that do not exit; add a timeout or run them in the background with `&` and kill them afterwards.
- Do not use the network (no go get, npm install, curl) unless the task requires it; dependencies are already present.
- Files under .qh/ belong to the harness. Read them when useful but do not edit them.

# Environment facts
- Go toolchain is installed; module downloads are disabled (GOPROXY=off), so use only the standard library and modules already in go.mod.
- `go test ./...` runs all tests; add `-run TestName` to focus and `-count=1` to bypass the test cache.

# Tool guidance
- read_file shows line numbers; they are not part of the file. Never copy the line-number prefix into old_text or file content.
- edit_file needs old_text to match exactly once, including indentation (Go uses tabs). If it fails, re-read the region and retry with the exact text.
- run output is capped; very long output is saved under .qh/spill/ and you can read_file it.
- Use grep to locate code instead of reading many whole files.
- delegate only for broad read-only investigations whose answer is short.

# Task
The INI parser in package `ini` has bugs: `go test ./...` fails. Fix the parser so it follows the format documented in the package comment of `ini/ini.go`. Do not change the tests in `ini/ini_test.go`; they describe correct behaviour. There may be bugs the existing tests do not cover, so check the documented format carefully.

# Workspace

It must exit 0. Run it yourself before calling finish.

The package comment documents the format, and the code has multiple deviations. Let me check the bugs:

1. Lines aren't trimmed before comment/empty checks (and `#` comments not handled at all)
2. Section names aren't lower-cased
3. `LastIndex` instead of first `=` for key/value split
4. Inline comment cut at any `;` (not requiring preceding whitespace, and `#` not handled), and applied to quoted values too
5. Quoted values have inner whitespace trimmed (should be preserved exactly)
6. Repeated keys don't overwrite

Let me fix the parser:
msg.reasoning_content:
Bugs based on the documented format:

1. Lines are first trimmed of surrounding whitespace; currently the check `line == "" || line[0] == ';'` is done before trimming. So "  # comment" or "  ;" fails. Fix: first trim the line.

2. Comments: lines starting with ';' or '#' (after trimming) are comments. Currently '#' is not checked.

3. Section names are lowercased; currently section is not lowercased. `section = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(...))`.

4. The first '=' separates the key and value; currently LastIndex is used. Fix: Index.

5. Values are trimmed; inline comments start with " ;" or " #" (whitespace followed by ; or #) inside a non-quoted value. Currently it cuts at any ';' even without whitespace, and it also cuts '#'? Actually it only cuts on ';', and only when j>=0 — but it should only cut when preceded by whitespace. Also for '#' — the documentation says inline comments start with " ;" or " #". So we need to find the first occurrence of " ;" or " #".

6. Quoted values: quotes are stripped, and the inner whitespace is preserved exactly. Currently it's doing TrimSpace on the inner content — this strips the inner whitespace. For `"  /srv  "` -> should be "  /srv  " but becomes "/srv". Fix: don't trim the inside.

Also order matters: for unquoted values, strip inline comments, then for quoted values, strip quotes and preserve inner whitespace. Note: for unquoted values the value is already trimmed; for quoted values after stripping quotes, we must not trim (preserve inner whitespace). But the documentation says "value is trimmed" then "a value wrapped in double quotes has its quotes stripped and the inner whitespace is preserved exactly." That is: trim the value, and if it is wrapped in quotes, strip the quotes without trimming the inside.

Also inline comments are only stripped for unquoted values; for quoted values, is there a chance that the content of a quoted value contains " ;"? The documentation says "inside a non-quoted value." That is: after trimming, check if wrapped in quotes; if yes, strip quotes (no inline comment stripping, no inner trimming). If not, look for " ;" or " #" and truncate at the first occurrence, then trim.

Wait, order: the value is first trimmed. If it starts with '"', is it "wrapped"? Probably both first and last character. Edge case: val == "\"" (length 1) is not wrapped.

7. Repeated keys overwrite; currently !exists skips — bug. Fix: just set.

Also regarding section: keys before any section go into section "" — already fine.

Also the section check: what if a line like "[foo" (no closing bracket) has "="? In that case it becomes a key line with key "[foo". The documentation says other lines are syntax errors. Hmm, "any other line is a syntax error" — lines that can't be parsed as key=value. A line "[foo" without '=' is already a syntax error. Then what about "[foo] extra"? line[0]=='[' but the last char is not ']', then it falls through to key=value parsing; if no '=', syntax error. That's probably fine.

Also section line check: currently it requires both the first and last character to be brackets. What about " [Server] " — after trimming it becomes "[Server]" so fine.

Also, the documentation says keys are lowercased and trimmed — fine.

One more subtle point: section lines are trimmed and lowercased. Currently trimming is done but not lowercased.

Also, comment check: after trimming, lines starting with ';' or '#' are ignored (both).

Also, should the scanner handle long lines? Not needed.

Rewriting the parse loop:

```go
for sc.Scan() {
    n++
    line := strings.TrimSpace(sc.Text())
    if line == "" || line[0] == ';' || line[0] == '#' {
        continue
    }
    if line[0] == '[' && line[len(line)-1] == ']' {
        section = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1]))
        continue
    }
    i := strings.Index(line, "=")
    if i < 0 {
        return nil, &SyntaxError{Line: n, Text: sc.Text()}
    }
    key := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line[:i]))
    val := strings.TrimSpace(line[i+1:])
    if len(val) >= 2 && val[0] == '"' && val[len(val)-1] == '"' {
        val = val[1 : len(val)-1]
    } else {
        if j := strings.Index(val, " ;"); j >= 0 {
            val = val[:j]
        } else if j := strings.Index(val, " #"); j >= 0 {
            val = val[:j]
        }
        val = strings.TrimSpace(val)
    }
    ...
    f[section][key] = val
}
```

I'll use the raw sc.Text() — actually the documentation says Text is the problematic line; the test doesn't check it. I'll keep the trimmed one… either is fine; using the trimmed one. Actually the original code was using the un-trimmed line. Doesn't matter. Use line (already trimmed) — hmm, in the original code, in the "=" branch `line` was the raw text. Let me use the trimmed version; it's fine.

Edge case: value wrapped in quotes — should we also strip inline comments? Documentation: "inside a non-quoted value" — so no.

Also empty section name "[]" — fine, it becomes "".

Another edge: a line like "key = " with an empty value — val = "" is fine.

Also `url = http://x/?a=b` — with Index instead of LastIndex, key="url", val="http://x/?a=b". Good.

Inline comment: "8080   ; inline comment" -> after trimming "8080   ; inline comment"; Index of " ;" -> cuts at the position of the space, then TrimSpace -> "8080". Good.
